subject: Cross-store gates: contract scope & ops alignment
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@pinecone.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Cross-store gates: draft scope and ops artifacts

Kimberly / Ben / team —

Thanks again for taking time today. Per our call, attaching a short packet that outlines the end-to-end behaviours we expect from the connector: replication semantics, cold-tier fallthrough, and the recommended failover for vector reads. Key asks from our side:

- Confirmation on data residency constraints (we noted EU customers will want S3-only fallthrough).
- Target SLA for read latency and acceptable tail latency for small/large vectors.
- Who owns snapshot/backup cadence and restoration runbooks in outage scenarios.

I've included a compatibility matrix and a short tech appendix (connector-capabilities-v2.pdf, connector-compat-matrix.csv). Can you review and flag any items that are blockers commercially or operationally?

We also sketched a commercial split for co-sell referrals + a modest revenue share for storage-anchored customers; happy to walk through numbers next week.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Gupta
Partner Engineering Manager, Pinecone
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@pinecone.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-store gates: draft scope and ops artifacts

Samir —

Appreciate the packet and the matrix. High-level notes after a quick pass (more detail below and in the attached ops_checklist.xlsx):

1) Residency: agree on S3-only fallback in EU, but we need explicit wording about what data flows into Pinecone-managed indexes vs customer-owned S3 buckets. Legal will want that in the MSA.
2) SLA: we can offer an endpoint SLA for hosted routes but not for cross-tenant storage fallthrough unless we control the snapshot cadence — suggesting a 99.9% read availability target for managed routes and a separate annex for fallthrough expectations.
3) Backups: ops to own the primary snapshot schedule; partner to provide a tested restore playbook (we should run one restore as a joint exercise in staging).

Next steps: Marissa, can you pick up the commercial split model and confirm if the referral revenue share is acceptable for our standard reseller program? Ben / Karthik — please review the technical failover plan in connector-compat-matrix.csv and flag any non-starters.

I've attached an ops checklist that maps responsibilities to owners. We'll use that as an appendix to the SOW.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ops_checklist.xlsx
From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com; Samir Gupta <samir@pinecone.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-store gates: draft scope and ops artifacts

Quick follow-up from my side — two technical clarifications before we lock scope: 

- Can Pinecone support non-blocking reads while a reindex or repair job is running on the S3-backed store? If not, we need to call that out as a maintenance window and define a max duration.
- For prefix/KV cache invalidation across regions, do you expect our runtime to push events or for Pinecone to pull deltas? The matrix notes both options but not our recommended default.

On the latter, if Pinecone prefers a pull model we should include a small batching window in the SLOs to avoid extremely chatty traffic.

Ben Carter
Principal Engineer, Indexing & Connectors
Redwood Inference

From: Mike Turner <mike@stratusai.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@pinecone.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-store gates: draft scope and ops artifacts

Hi all —

Thanks for the detailed notes. StratusAI is comfortable taking the SOW and the initial joint restore runbook on as part of our delivery scope — attached is a first-pass SOW (SOW-draft.pdf) that lines up responsibilities:

- StratusAI: co-deliver connector deployment, run the first restore test, provide training to customer ops.
- Pinecone: provide support for index lifecycle tooling and assist on tests that target large vector tables.
- Redwood: owner of the in-product routing policy and billing split.

Two asks from our side before we sign:
1) Clear escalation path and a named POC for on-call during the staging restore exercise.
2) Confirmation that the referral revenue share is not below your standard channel floor (Marissa — can you confirm?)

If these two items are happy, we can push a draft DocuSign link by EOD and target a joint staging restore the week of Dec 13.

Thanks — Mike Turner
Director, Strategic Partnerships
StratusAI

Attachment: SOW-draft.pdf
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike@stratusai.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@pinecone.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cross-store gates: draft scope and ops artifacts

Mike / Samir —

This looks good and thanks for the SOW. Quick answers and decisions from our side: 

- Escalation/POC: assigning Karthik Iyer as technical POC for the staging restore (karthik_iyer@redwood.com). He will coordinate the on-call rota and the exact rollback triggers.
- Revenue share: Marissa confirms we're within channel floor for initial pilots; she'll follow up with the final commercial wording and send a DocuSign link for the SOW.
- Ben: we'll take the non-blocking reads as a maintenance-window item — please add a max window (we suggest 30 minutes) and procedures for customer notification.

Marissa — please open a HubSpot deal record (HD-3245) for this co-sell and add the SOW + ops checklist to the documents tab. Target: DocuSign out today, joint staging restore week of Dec 13.

Thanks everyone — moving to Marissa for handoff.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
